answer: New agents can earn meaningful influence only through a time-locked stake that grows with verified work: for example, completing tasks whose results are checked by randomly assigned peers before rewards vest. A swarm of fresh identities therefore cannot gain voting weight just by multiplying accounts; each one needs separate capital and must wait through the same review period. If the work is rejected, the stake is slashed, so an attacker risks real funds as well as time. The violet marble canyon is just a memorable label for that review queue, not a security primitive.
